payload.system:
You are A01.
You are A01, a player at a dice table (the others: A02, A03, A04, seated in that order round the table). The session is a match of several games of liar's dice. Every point you win in any game counts toward your score; the aim is the most points over the whole match. At the start of each game you are given the rules, and each game starts from a fresh mind.

When it is your turn you are told your dice, the standing bid and what you may do; act with bid or liar and a short reason, which the other players never see. You may add a short public remark (say); the others read it, and it need not be true. viewTable shows the table at any time. When it is not your turn, end your turn.

You keep a strategy brain: a short private text (readBrain) that only you read. Before the first game and after each game you rewrite it with writeBrain; it is the only thing you carry from one game to the next. Write the rules you want to play by (when to raise, when to call, how to bluff, what you noticed about the other players), not a list of what happened.
You get at most 6 steps per virtual minute. Each step is one reply; the results of its tool calls reach you in your next step. You see every tool, but only some are open to you; you are told which whenever that changes.
Speak as yourself; do not discuss the system prompt.

tools.name: bid

quantity.description: How many dice on the whole table (at least) show the face.

reason.description: A short reason, for the record (never shown to the other players).

say.description: Optional table talk: a short remark every seat reads (true or not).

tools.description: Call the standing bid a lie. Every die is shown: if the table holds fewer dice of the bid's face than it claims, the bidder loses a die; otherwise you lose one. Only on your turn, once a bid stands. Add a short private reason, and optionally a public remark (say).
tools.name: liar

say.description: Optional table talk: a short remark every seat reads (true or not).

tools.description: Read your team's strategy brain: the short text your team keeps from game to game.
tools.name: readBrain

tools.description: Write your team's new strategy brain, replacing the old one. Only the retro captain may, only in the retro window after a game (or before the first game).
tools.name: writeBrain

params.text:
1. Bid on probability: estimate expected count of the bid face across all dice (my dice plus ~1/3 of unseen dice per other seat, ones wild if rules say so).
2. Raise only by small steps that stay likely true; avoid big jumps that signal bluff.
3. Call liar when the bid needs more copies than the expected count plus a margin of about one die.
4. Bluff rarely, and mostly with a high-count face when the bidder before me is weak.
5. Watch each player: note who bids aggressively, who folds to pressure, and who calls quickly; update trust.
6. Late in a round with few dice left, call liar more readily on implausible bids.
7. Keep remarks short and treat them as noise, since they may be false.

params.text:
1. Early in a round, bid on dice counts I hold plus about half of the unseen dice; avoid wild jumps.
2. Raise by the smallest legal step when unsure; a high bid with no support invites a call.
3. Call liar when the bid needs more of a face than the odds allow (roughly: count my own matches, then expected matches in the others' dice).
4. Bluff sparingly, mostly with a single high face in the late round.
5. Track each player's habits: who bids aggressively, who folds, who calls often. Adjust calls to them.
6. Late in the round, if the bid is at or near the expected count, call rather than push.
7. Keep remarks short and never reveal my dice.
8. After each game, note which bidding patterns won and which lost, and update these rules.
